html:
Turku Cathedral, in the old capital of Finland, was consecrated in 1300. It is the mother church of the Finnish Lutheran church and the country's national shrine.

Swedish kings and the church brought Finland under Swedish rule in the 1200s, in campaigns later called crusades. Turku, on the southwest coast, became the seat of the bishop and the main town, with a royal castle at the harbour. Finland was part of Sweden for about six hundred years.

The cathedral was rebuilt after fires, the worst in 1827, which destroyed most of Turku. That fire helped confirm the move of the capital to Helsinki. The bishop Mikael Agricola worked here during the Reformation. See Finland and Christianity.
sum: Turku Cathedral, in the old capital of Finland, was consecrated in 1300. It is the mother church of the Finnish Lutheran church and the country's national shrine.
